text:
Priya Desai: hi team, first week here! Trying to get kubectl working. I downloaded the onboarding kubeconfig from the portal and also have my personal config from home. After merging them I get TLS handshake errors when hitting the dev cluster. Any idea what I messed up? :confused:

Priya Desai: steps I took:
1) downloaded `onboard-kubeconfig.yaml` to `~/work/onboard`
2) ran `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/work/onboard kubectl config view --merge --flatten > ~/.kube/merged`
3) `mv ~/.kube/merged ~/.kube/config`

Priya Desai: error when running `kubectl get namespaces`: `Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`

DevEx Bot: welcome Priya! :tada: Common causes: mismatched cluster server URLs, or your merged file has the wrong certificate-authority-data entry overridden. Quick checks:
• `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'` to see which server current context points to
• `kubectl config view --raw` will show `certificate-authority-data` (base64). If your personal config had a `certificate-authority` file path, merging might have left a file path that doesn't exist on your laptop.

Alex G.: echoing DevEx Bot — I ran into this. If one kubeconfig references a local CA file (e.g., `/etc/kube/pki/ca.pem`) and you merge, the merged file might still include `certificate-authority: /etc/...` which breaks on different machines. Replace those with `certificate-authority-data` (base64 blob) or update to point to a file that exists.

Priya Desai: here's my cluster entry snippet from `kubectl config view --raw` (sanitized):```
clusters:
- name: dev.reds
  cluster:
    server: https://dev.reds.internal:6443
    certificate-authority: /Users/priya/.keys/dev-ca.pem
- name: personal-minikube
  cluster:
    server: https://192.168.99.100:8443
    certificate-authority-data: REDACTEDBASE64
```

DevEx Bot: yep that's it — the merged config kept `certificate-authority` path for the dev cluster which doesn't exist on your laptop. Two options:
1) Replace the `certificate-authority` line with `certificate-authority-data` using the CA file from the onboarding bundle: `base64 -i /path/to/onboard/ca.pem | tr -d '\n'` and paste the output as the certificate-authority-data value (backup your config first).
2) Put the CA file at the same path `/Users/priya/.keys/dev-ca.pem` and ensure permissions are correct (600).

Alex G.: also check the `cluster.server` URLs. If your company VPN is required to reach `dev.reds.internal`, make sure you're connected. TLS errors can be misleading if route is blocked. `curl -v https://dev.reds.internal:6443` can give more context.

Priya Desai: I found the CA in the onboarding zip (thanks). I replaced the path with certificate-authority-data and re-ran `kubectl get ns` — now I get `Error from server (Forbidden): namespaces is forbidden: User "priya@company" cannot list resource "namespaces" in API group "" at the cluster scope`

Priya Desai: so progress! I assume this is RBAC — who should I ping for a quick grant to the onboarding group?

DevEx Bot: ping @onboarding (Onboarding Bot) — usually new hires are added to `group:eng-onboarding` which has namespace-reader RoleBinding in `onboard-*` namespaces. If not, file a request with `#help` or mention an oncall platform engineer.

Onboarding Bot: Hi Priya — congrats and welcome! :sparkles: I can check your group membership. Please paste the output of `kubectl config view --minify --raw | grep -E "user:|name:" -A2` (remove tokens) and I will validate. Also confirm which namespace you need access to (e.g., `onboard-priya`).

Priya Desai: pasted below (sanitized):```
users:
- name: priya@company (auth-provider: oidc)
contexts:
- name: onboard-priya@dev.reds
  context:
    cluster: dev.reds
    namespace: onboard-priya
    user: priya@company
```

Onboarding Bot: Thanks — you are not yet in `eng-onboarding`. I'll create a temporary RoleBinding for `user:priya@company` to `Role:onboard-namespace-admin` in `onboard-priya` for 48 hours. If you need longer, let me know and @devex can open a ticket for permanent group add.

Alex G.: FYI when people merge configs I often recommend keeping company kubeconfigs in a separate file and using `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/work/onboard/onboard-kubeconfig.yaml` until everything is working. Avoid overwriting `~/.kube/config` unless you want to; the `KUBECONFIG` env var is transient for that shell session.

Priya Desai: that would have saved me a headache :joy: thanks everyone — CA fix + temporary RBAC binding worked. I can list namespaces now. Would appreciate a short note in DevEx about the `certificate-authority` vs `certificate-authority-data` merge gotcha.

DevEx Bot: noted — will add a short tip to the DevEx onboarding doc. Welcome again Priya! :wave:
